items.title: DDP for Home Assistant
items.text:
A Home Assistant custom integration that drives DDP (Distributed Display Protocol) pixel controllers, such as the Minleon NDB-Pro, as native light entities. Each controller is one device with one light per output (a Minleon NDB-Pro adds a second device for its built-in effects and palette). Every light supports on/off, brightness, RGB color (RGBW on 4-channel pixels), and an effect list, so Home Assistant scenes can capture and replay it.

All protocol code lives in aioddp, and Minleon NDB-Pro control in pyminleon; this integration only maps them onto Home Assistant.

items.title: Guides
items.text:
• Installation — install with HACS or by hand, add a controller, reconfigure or remove it.
  • Configuration — controller types, options, and how state is kept up to date.
  • Entities — the lights, effects, patterns, NDB-Pro scenes and colors, actions, and automation examples.

items.title: Supported devices
items.text:
Device Support Minleon NDB-Pro with Rainmin RGB+ pixels The reference device. DDP lights plus the Scenes light, ddp.recall_preset, and ddp.set_colors Any other DDP v1 controller (UDP port 4048) Generic DDP: one light per output, or one light for the whole strip. Not tested beyond the DDP spec

RGB and RGBW pixels are supported. DDP is send-only, so Home Assistant cannot read a controller's state back over DDP; see Known limitations. See aioddp's compatibility notes for which controllers have been exercised.

items.title: Use cases
items.text:
• Run a roofline in a solid warm white most nights and a chase or rainbow effect for holidays, from dashboards or scenes.
  • Let the NDB-Pro play the shows stored on it on a schedule (sunset to 23:00) while Home Assistant stays in charge of the on/off times.
  • Take a section of the strip over for a one-off alert color (for example a doorbell flash) and hand it back after.

items.title: Known limitations
items.text:
• One DDP sender per controller. DDP has no priority or arbitration. If FPP, xLights, or anything else is driving the controller, stop it before using these lights, or the two fight frame by frame.
  • DDP takes over the NDB-Pro, and it gives up after about 20 s. DDP data overrides the controller's built-in effect at once; about 20 s after DDP stops it falls back to it, even mid solid color. The keepalive (default 1 s) prevents this; with keepalive 0 a solid color reverts after about 20 s.
  • Recalling a preset overwrites the controller's current colors with the preset's. The integration never writes the controller's saved settings.
  • Segment light state is assumed. Changes made elsewhere (the controller's web UI, another sender) are not seen.
  • Setup cannot verify the controller over DDP. It only checks that a UDP socket opens; a wrong host looks fine until a frame is sent and nothing lights up.
  • The Scenes light needs the controller's HTTP UI on port 80 and only exists for vendor controller types.
  • The layout is read when the entry is added and on Reconfigure, never at startup. If you re-patch outputs or change the controller's input mode, reconfigure the entry.
  • White needs a 4-channel input mode. The NDB-Pro must be set to a 4-channel (RGBW) input mode in its own UI for the entry to be RGBW; reconfigure the entry after changing it. In a 3-channel mode the controller derives white itself and the lights stay RGB.
  • Animated effects ignore white. breathe, chase, twinkle, and rainbow render RGB: on an RGBW light they use the color's red, green, and blue and leave the white LEDs off. Solid colors and palette carry white.
  • No discovery. DDP has no discovery protocol, so controllers are added by host.
  • No brand images yet, so the integration shows Home Assistant's placeholder icon.

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.text:
Symptom What to check Lights do not react Host is right; UDP 4048 is not blocked between Home Assistant and the controller; nothing else is sending DDP to it; the output is patched on the controller. The brightness cap (default 60%) may also make colors dimmer than expected Colors are wrong (red and green swapped, ...) Set Color order in the options to match the pixels A solid color turns into the controller's own effect after about 20 s The keepalive is off or too long; set it to 1 s Scenes light is unavailable The controller's web UI (TCP 80) is not answering. The DDP lights are unaffected; the Scenes light recovers on the next 30 s poll The controller has a new IP address Reconfigure the entry and enter the new host (give the controller a DHCP reservation to avoid this) ddp.recall_preset or ddp.set_colors is refused The target is a segment light, or the entry is Generic DDP, which has no Scenes light. ddp.set_colors also refuses more than 5 colors, a component outside 0-255, or a name other than cool_white / warm_white ddp.set_pattern is refused The target is the Scenes light, the effect takes no colors (rainbow), or a params value is out of range or not a parameter of that effect (the message names it) A color with a white value is refused The entry is RGB, or the effect is not palette (the animated effects render RGB only). For white, set the NDB-Pro to a 4-channel input mode and reconfigure the entry An output light turned off by itself All outputs was turned on; it owns the pixels of every output until an output light is turned on again

To report a problem, include the downloaded diagnostics and debug logs:

logger:
  logs:
    custom_components.ddp: debug
    aioddp: debug
    pyminleon: debug

items.title: Controller types
items.text:
Type Lights Generic DDP One DDP light per output. Works with any DDP controller; nothing else is created Minleon NDB-Pro The DDP lights, plus a controller device with the Scenes light and the ddp.recall_preset and ddp.set_colors actions (see NDB-Pro built-in scenes)

The stored type decides: nothing probes the controller at startup. Adding another vendor's controller means one entry in the controller type registry (custom_components/ddp/controller.py) backed by that vendor's library.

items.title: Pixel type
items.text: The entry's pixel type (RGB or RGBW) decides every DDP light's color mode: RGBW entries use rgbw_color. An NDB-Pro reports it from its input mode, so it must be set to a 4-channel mode in its own UI for the entry to be RGBW; then Reconfigure the entry to re-read the layout (pixel count, type, and outputs). Details are in RGBW.

items.title: Options
items.text:
Option Default Notes Brightness cap 60% Applied to every frame, effects included. Lower it to protect power supplies Color order RGB / RGBW Channel order the pixels expect Effect frame rate 30 fps 1 to 60 Keepalive interval 1 s Re-sends the current frame so the controller doesn't fall back to its built-in effect; 0 turns it off, otherwise at least 0.5 s

Saving options reloads the entry.

items.title: Data updates
items.text:
• Segment lights never poll. DDP has no read path, so Home Assistant's state is the truth: it is restored after a restart and, if the light was on, sent again. Sends are local UDP and raise an error in the action if the socket fails.
  • The Scenes light polls the controller's web UI every 30 seconds and again right after each command it sends. If the controller does not answer, only the Scenes light becomes unavailable (logged once, and again when it is back); the DDP lights keep working.
  • Patterns are kept across restarts. A DDP light restores its pattern with the rest of its state.

items.title: Diagnostics
items.text: Settings > Devices & services > DDP Pixel Controller > Download diagnostics includes the entry, the DDP sender's counters, and, for an NDB-Pro, the Scenes light's state and palette and the controller's config and status documents. The host, IP addresses, MAC address, and Wi-Fi name are redacted.

items.title: Lights
items.text:
Entity What it does Output N light (one per output; All for a manually described strip) On/off, brightness, RGB color (RGBW color for an RGBW entry), the aioddp effects, and multi-color patterns (ddp.set_pattern). Sends DDP; its state is assumed All outputs light (only when the controller has more than one output) The same as an output light, over the whole strip: a pattern or effect runs on across the outputs in one DDP frame Scenes light (vendor controller types only, on the controller device) Selects the controller's built-in effects and shows, brightness maps to its intensity. Its palette is the colors and background attributes, set with ddp.set_colors. Polled

Devices. The output lights and All outputs are on the DDP device, named after the entry. A vendor controller type adds a controller device named after the entry and the type (for example "Front Yard Minleon NDB-Pro"), connected through the DDP device, with the Scenes light on it.

Actions: ddp.set_pattern (DDP lights: the outputs and All outputs), and ddp.recall_preset and ddp.set_colors (NDB-Pro Scenes light only). Home Assistant's light.turn_on and light.turn_off work on every light, and scenes capture the segment lights. The integration provides no triggers or conditions.

All outputs and the output lights share pixels, so only one of them owns a pixel at a time. Turning All outputs on stops the output lights' effects and shows them off, without sending anything; turning an output light on does the same to All outputs. Nothing is blanked: the newly turned-on light simply draws over its own pixels, and an output that All outputs had lit keeps that frame until something else sends to it.

items.title: RGBW
items.text: When the entry's pixel type is RGBW (the controller reports 4-channel input, or you chose RGBW when describing the strip), every DDP light uses Home Assistant's RGBW color mode: rgbw_color sets red, green, blue, and white, and white reaches the pixels' white LEDs. The default look is the white channel alone, [0, 0, 0, 255]. Solid colors and palette patterns carry white; the animated effects use red, green, and blue only. An NDB-Pro must be in a 4-channel input mode for this (see Pixel type); an RGB entry refuses a color with a white value.

items.title: Effects
items.text: The effect list comes from aioddp: breathe, chase, twinkle, rainbow, palette. The effect off means a solid color. The light's RGB color drives each effect's main color where it has one (for example the chase color or the breathe color, or the one palette color); brightness scales the whole effect. breathe, chase, twinkle, and rainbow ignore white on an RGBW light.

items.title: Patterns
items.text:
ddp.set_pattern gives a DDP light several colors at once: by default the palette effect repeats them in fixed blocks (block_size pixels each, so two colors with block size 1 alternate pixel by pixel). It can also hand the colors to chase (its lit groups cycle through them), or to breathe and twinkle, which use the first color. params sets the effect's other parameters, such as the chase speed; a bad value is refused with the parameter named. The light's effect shows the rendering effect, and the pattern is kept across restarts and a bare light.turn_on. A later light.turn_on with a color replaces the pattern with that one color; choosing another effect drops it.

On an RGBW entry a pattern color may be [r, g, b, w] (an [r, g, b] color gets white 0), with palette only; the other effects render RGB and refuse a white value, as does an RGB entry.

items.title: NDB-Pro built-in scenes
items.text:
A controller of type Minleon NDB-Pro (detected from its status model NDBPRO, or chosen by hand) gets one more light on a second device, " Minleon NDB-Pro": Scenes. It drives the controller's own built-in effects over its HTTP UI instead of sending DDP. Entity IDs below assume the entry is named "NDBPRO" (the title discovery gives it unless the controller reports a name), so the lights are light.ndbpro_minleon_ndb_pro_scenes, light.ndbpro_output_1, and so on; check yours on the device pages. (A Scenes light created before the controller device existed keeps its entity ID, for example light.ndbpro_scenes.)

  • Its effect list is the controller's: Show1 and Show2 play the shows stored on the controller; the rest (Test, Bands, Glow, ...) are its built-in patterns. Brightness maps to the controller's intensity (0-100%).
  • light.turn_off selects the controller's Off and also blanks any segment light that is on, so the house goes dark.
  • A bare light.turn_on brings back the last scene, also after a Home Assistant restart. Startup never commands the controller; the light polls the controller every 30 s and shows what it is actually running.
  • ddp.recall_preset plays one of the 20 stored presets (1-10 are slots of Show 1, 11-20 of Show 2).
  • ddp.set_colors sets the palette the built-in effects draw from: up to 5 custom colors and a background. The colors and background attributes show the palette as the controller reports it ([0, 0, 0] is an empty slot). cool_white and warm_white select the controller's white LEDs (it maps #feffff to cool white and pure white to warm white); an empty list clears the palette, so the controller picks random colors. Setting colors does not turn the Scenes light on or take the pixels from a DDP light, and it is not saved to the controller's flash.

Segment lights vs. scenes. DDP data overrides the controller's built-in effect immediately, and about 20 s after DDP stops the controller falls back to it. So the two kinds of light take turns:

  • Turning on a scene (or recalling a preset) first turns every DDP light (the outputs and All outputs) off without sending black and stops DDP, so the scene shows at once.
  • Turning a segment light on takes the pixels over again. While any segment light is on, the keepalive (default 1 s) keeps re-sending its frame so the controller does not fall back mid-color; with keepalive 0 a solid color reverts to the built-in effect after about 20 s.
  • When the last segment light turns off, DDP stops; about 20 s later the controller's own scene (or Off) is back.

items.title: Actions
items.text:
Action Target Fields ddp.set_pattern An output light or All outputs colors (required: 1-16 colors, each [r, g, b] 0-255, or [r, g, b, w] on an RGBW entry with palette), block_size (pixels per color block, default 1; palette only), effect (palette by default, or chase, breathe, twinkle), params (the effect's other parameters, for example {"speed": 4}), brightness (1-255) ddp.recall_preset A Scenes light preset (1-20; 1-10 are slots of Show 1, 11-20 of Show 2) ddp.set_colors A Scenes light colors (required: 0-5 colors for palette slots 1-5, each [r, g, b] 0-255 or cool_white / warm_white; the remaining slots are emptied, and an empty list lets the controller pick random colors), background ([r, g, b]; left as it is when omitted) light.turn_on / light.turn_off Any light of this integration Segment lights: brightness, rgb_color (rgbw_color on an RGBW entry), effect. Scenes light: brightness, effect

ddp.set_pattern on the Scenes light, and ddp.recall_preset or ddp.set_colors on a segment light, are refused. Recalling a preset overwrites the controller's current colors with the preset's. Actions raise an error when a send fails, the effect is unknown or takes no colors, a pattern parameter is invalid, a pattern color has a white value the entry or effect cannot show, or the controller does not answer.

items.title: Examples: scenes on a schedule
items.text:
Schedule the controller's stored scenes with plain automations against the Scenes light:

automation:
  - alias: Show 1 at sunset
    triggers:
      - trigger: sun
        event: sunset
        offset: "-00:15:00"
    actions:
      - action: light.turn_on
        target:
          entity_id: light.ndbpro_minleon_ndb_pro_scenes
        data:
          effect: Show1
          brightness_pct: 80

  - alias: Holiday preset on weekends
    triggers:
      - trigger: time
        at: "18:00:00"
    conditions:
      - condition: time
        weekday: [sat, sun]
    actions:
      - action: ddp.recall_preset
        target:
          entity_id: light.ndbpro_minleon_ndb_pro_scenes
        data:
          preset: 3

  - alias: Lights off at 23:00
    triggers:
      - trigger: time
        at: "23:00:00"
    actions:
      - action: light.turn_off
        target:
          entity_id: light.ndbpro_minleon_ndb_pro_scenes

Turning the Scenes light off blanks the DDP segment lights too, so the 23:00 automation is all you need for "off".

Home Assistant scenes still work for the DDP segment lights; a scene captures each light's state (on/off, brightness, color, effect):

scene:
  - name: Roofline warm chase
    entities:
      light.ndbpro_output_1:
        state: "on"
        brightness: 200
        rgb_color: [255, 140, 40]
        effect: chase
      light.ndbpro_output_2:
        state: "on"
        brightness: 180
        rgb_color: [255, 0, 0]
        effect: "off" # solid color; quote it, a bare off is a YAML boolean

Activate it from an automation with scene.turn_on. After a Home Assistant restart, each segment light restores its last state and, if it was on, sends it again.

items.title: Examples: controller colors
items.text:
The controller's Fixed Colors effect in warm white and red, every other color (slots 1-4; slot 5 is emptied):

- action: ddp.set_colors
  target:
    entity_id: light.ndbpro_minleon_ndb_pro_scenes
  data:
    colors: ["warm_white", [255, 0, 0], "warm_white", [255, 0, 0]]
- action: light.turn_on
  target:
    entity_id: light.ndbpro_minleon_ndb_pro_scenes
  data:
    effect: Fixed Colors

Clear the palette so the controller picks random colors:

action: ddp.set_colors
target:
  entity_id: light.ndbpro_minleon_ndb_pro_scenes
data:
  colors: []

items.title: Examples: patterns
items.text:
Alternate red and green pixel by pixel across both outputs, as one continuous pattern:

action: ddp.set_pattern
target:
  entity_id: light.ndbpro_all_outputs
data:
  colors: [[255, 0, 0], [0, 255, 0]]
  block_size: 1
  brightness: 200

Red, white, and blue blocks of five pixels on one output, then a moving version with chase:

- action: ddp.set_pattern
  target:
    entity_id: light.ndbpro_output_1
  data:
    colors: [[255, 0, 0], [255, 255, 255], [0, 0, 255]]
    block_size: 5
- action: ddp.set_pattern
  target:
    entity_id: light.ndbpro_output_1
  data:
    colors: [[255, 0, 0], [255, 255, 255], [0, 0, 255]]
    effect: chase
    params:
      speed: 4
      spacing: 6
      width: 3

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text:
• Home Assistant 2026.10.0 or later.
  • The controller reachable from Home Assistant over UDP port 4048 and, for the Scenes light, TCP port 80.
  • git available to Home Assistant: the two libraries are installed from pinned git commits (aioddp is not yet published to PyPI).

items.title: HACS (custom repository)
items.text:
1. In HACS, open the menu and choose Custom repositories.
  2. Add https://github.com/amattas/hass-ddp with type Integration.
  3. Install DDP Pixel Controller and restart Home Assistant.

items.title: Manual
items.text:
1. Copy the custom_components/ddp folder of the repository into <config>/custom_components/.
  2. Restart Home Assistant.

items.title: Add a controller
items.text:
1. Settings > Devices & services > Add integration > DDP Pixel Controller.
  2. Enter the controller's IP address or hostname.
  3. Home Assistant asks the controller for its output layout (a DDP query, then the controller's own API if its type is known to serve one) and checks which kind of controller it is.
  4. Pick the Controller type. The detected type is preselected; Generic DDP is always offered.
  5. If a layout was found, one light is created per active output ("Output 1", "Output 2", ...). If not, enter the total pixel count and pixel type (RGB or RGBW) and one light covering the whole strip is created.
Field Step Notes Host Add IP address or hostname. One entry per host; adding the same host again is refused Controller type Add, Reconfigure Generic DDP or a vendor type (see Controller types) Pixel count Add (manual only) Total pixels the controller drives Pixel type Add (manual only) RGB or RGBW (channels per pixel)

DDP is send-only UDP with no acknowledgement, so setup can only check that a socket opens. Setup never sends a frame, and reloading or removing the integration never blanks the lights.

items.title: Reconfigure
items.text:
Reconfigure on the integration entry changes the host (for example after a new DHCP lease) or the controller type, and re-reads the output layout the same way adding does (a DDP query, then the controller type's own API). The form shows the stored pixel type and the layout the controller reports now. When it reports one, the entry stores its pixel type (RGB or RGBW), outputs, and pixel count; so after switching an NDB-Pro between a 3-channel and a 4-channel input mode, reconfigure the entry to follow it. Outputs that are still there keep their lights; an output that is gone loses its light (and with a single output left, All outputs goes too). A color order option that does not fit the new pixel type is reset to the default. When the controller reports no layout, the stored one is kept.

The entry reloads and keeps its devices, entities, and history. Choosing Generic DDP removes the controller device and its Scenes light.

items.title: Removal
items.text:
1. Settings > Devices & services > DDP Pixel Controller, open the entry's menu and choose Delete.
  2. If you installed with HACS, remove DDP Pixel Controller in HACS and restart Home Assistant; for a manual install, delete <config>/custom_components/ddp and restart.

Removing the entry stops the integration's frames but does not blank the lights; the controller falls back to its own effect (about 20 s on an NDB-Pro). Turn the lights off first if you want them dark.
